This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 30.12.2023 at about 11-00 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding in his Motor cycle bearing No.KA-41-EF-0820 from Magadi Main road and when he reached near Marenahalli Village, Bangalore Magadi Road, Tavarekere, Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk, Bangalore, at that time the driver of Goods Carrier vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF-3492 and car bearing No.KA-05-MZ-7169 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Samraksha Hospital, Honaganahatti Magadi Main Road, Bangalore and from there,
he was shifted to Sri Lakshmi Multi-Speciality Hospital, Sunkadakatte, Bangalore wherein admitted as an inpatient for eight days.

He was working as a Farmer by profession and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability, he is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability & loss of income.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2/the Insurer of Goods Carrier vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF-3492 has filed written statement and contended that the driver of the Goods Carrier vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle was not having valid permit as on the date of accident and same is recorded in the charge sheet.

It is further contended that the Goods Carrier vehicle was not involved in the accident and that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the accident, caused by unknown vehicle which is evident from the complaint lodged by the petitioner after 5 days of the accident.

It is further contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the petitioner, who was fallen from the motorcycle which was proceeding near Tavarekere road on the middle of road without having proper look on the vehicular movements on the road and without noticing the oncoming vehicles he suddenly tried to cross the road and met with an accident.
5. In spite of the service of notice, the respondent No.1, respondent No.3 and respondent No.4 have remained absent.

Hence they were placed ex-parte.
6.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves

that he had sustained grievous injuries on account of Road Traffic Accident on 30.12.2023 at about 11-00 am., on Marenahalli Village,
Bangalore Magadi Road, Tavarekere Hobali, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Goods Carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-51- AF-3492 and Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05- MZ-7169?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7.
The petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.

On the other hand, Chandrakala- Superintendent, RTO, Bangalore is examined as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

sentences.text: 3 10. Issue No.1:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of Goods Carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF-3492 and Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05- MZ-7169, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 30.12.2023 at about 11-00 a.m. when the petitioner was proceeding in his Motor cycle bearing No.KA-41-EF-0820 from Magadi Main road, near Marenahalli Village, on Bangalore - Magadi Road, Tavarekere, Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk, Bangalore, at that time the Goods Carrier vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF-3492 and Car bearing No.KA-05-MZ-7169 (herein after called the offending vehicles) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, Spot mahazar, two Notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act, reply given thereon, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet, etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Purushotham.D.V., case has been registered against the drivers of car bearing No.KA-05-MZ-7169 and Goods Carrier vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF-3492 in Crime No.0005/2024 of Tavarekere Traffic Police Station, for the offence punishable under section 279 & 337 of IPC.
The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicles for the offence punishable under section 279 & 337 of IPC and u/Sec.196 of IMV Act.
13. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 at the out set has disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

It is submitted by the learned counsel that as per the own case of the petitioner their insured vehicle has not touched to the vehicle of the petitioner and it is the Car which was involved in the accident has dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner and that since the vehicle of the respondent no.3 had no insurance policy, in order to get unlawful enrichment at the cost of respondent no.2 they have falsely implicated their insured vehicle in the case.

The learned counsel in further has argued that, as per the evidence of the petitioner three vehicles involved in the accident was proceeding on the same direction but, the PW.1 in his evidence has deposed that, the Car and insured vehicle hit to the motor cycle on its front portion, hence, there is contradiction in the evidence of PW.1.
The learned counsel in further has argued about the delay in lodging the complaint.
14. So far as the delay in lodging the complaint is concerned, it is true that the accident in question has occurred on 30-12-2023 at about 11-00 a.m.
The complaint came to be lodged on 4-1-2024.

In the complaint and in the FIR reason for delay has been explained stating that, the driver of two offending vehicles have assured of meeting the medical expenses of the petitioner and later on, they have turned back from their words which constrained him to lodge the complaint at belated stage.

15. If the medical records are perused, soon after the accident, petitioner has taken treatment at Samraksha hospital and later at Sri Lakshmi Multi specialty hospital on the H/o injury sustained in the accident.
If the written statement filed by the respondent no.2 is read in whole they have not Krishnappa vs S R K Enterpirses on 5 February, 2026

Hence, the petitioner has satisfactorily explained the reason for delay in lodging the complaint.

16. If the complaint, evidence of the PW.1 and entire police records are perused, no where the petitioner has stated that his vehicle and offending vehicles was proceeding on the same direction and hit to his vehicle.

The PW.1 has deposed that, at the time of accident he was proceeding on the left side of the road, at that time, Goods carrier vehicle and Car came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to his vehicle.
The Pw.1 in categorical terms has deposed that, at the first instance the Goods carrier hit to the Car and the Car in turn hit to his vehicle.
If the IMV report is perused, the front left side wheel bolt of the Goods Carrier was rubbed.

So far as the Car involved in the accident is concerned, the left side portion of the front bumper and grill was damaged, the right side portion of the rear door was damaged and rubbing mark was found on the front right side door.
So far as the vehicle of the petitioner is concerned, front shape was damaged, front wheel mud guard was damaged, front fork was bent.

From the aforesaid damages caused to the three vehicles it can be said that the Goods Carrier at the first instance hit to the Car and the Car in turn hit to the front portion of the motor cycle, hence only the front portion of the Goods carrier, the front and rear portion of the Car and the front portion of the motor vehicle was damaged.
If the spot mahazar is perused, the width of the road at the spot of the accident is nearly 28 ft.
There is clear mention in the spot mahazar regarding the occurrence of accident on the left side of the road.

It clearly proves that,
the offending vehicles which came from opposite direction by taking the vehicle on the right side of the road dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner.
Hence, the driver of both the vehicles have contributed negligency.

So far as the quantum of negligence contributed by the Goods carrier is concerned, as observed supra at the first instance because of the rash and negligent driving it hit to the Car and the Car in turn hit to the motor cycle.
Hence, higher degree of negligence has to be attributed to the driver of Goods carrier.
Hence, the negligence contributed by the driver of lorry is assessed at the ratio of 80% and of the driver of the car at the ratio of 20%.
Accordingly issue no.1 is answered in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., wound certificate and discharge summary which are at Ex.P5 and Ex.P11.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at Sri Lakshmi Multi- Specialty Hospital on 31.12.2023 to 06.01.2024 for a period of 7 days.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained three injuries of which injury no.1 and 2 are simple in nature.
So far as injury no.3 is concerned, Ex.P5 does not disclose the nature of injury whether it is simple or grievous in nature.
In the Ex.P5 it is noted that the opinion regarding the third injury has to be obtained by the concerned person from the hospital where he was initially treated i.e., from Samraksha hospital.
Admittedly the wound certificate of Samraksha hospital is not produced.
Further, the petitioner has not examined the Medical officer of Samraksha hospital, who has given treatment to him.
Hence there is no material to assess the nature of third injury sustained by the petitioner.
Since petitioner has taken treatment for 7 days and has incurred medical expenses to the tune of Rs.98,848/- it can be said that injury no.3 is grievous in nature.

sentences.text: Since the petitioner has not examined the medical officer who has given treatment and there is no evidence on record to say that petitioner has suffered permanent disability, there is no loss of future income.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.

19. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury and two simple injuries Hence taking into consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc., it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
20. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced medical bills for sum of Rs.98,848/- at Ex.P.8.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for Rs.98,848./- under the head medical expenses.
21. It is stated that petitioner was aged about 55 years.
He was Farmer by profession and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
In order to prove the same the petitioner has not produced any documents.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner,
taken the income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
22.
The petitioner has sustained three injuries and has taken treatment for 7 days as inpatient at Sri Lakshmi Multi-Speciality Hospital.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 3 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation, this court takes the loss of income during the laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for 3 month.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.49,500/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.

23. Further for 7 days of hospitalization at Sri Lakshmi Multi-Specialty, Bangalore and for his taking follow up treatment in the said hospital, requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment, for follow-ups has incurred traveling expenses, he has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.30,000/-.
24.
The petitioner at his age of 55 years has suffered grievous injury which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/-.

Thus Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
Sl. Heads Amount in No. rupees 1.
Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000-00 2.
Medical expenses Rs. 98,848-00 3. Loss of income during laid up Rs. 49,500-00  period
4. Towards incidental expenses Rs. 30,000-00 Krishnappa vs S R K Enterpirses on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152069981/

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,48,348/-.
25.

As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that Goods carrier bearing No.KA-51-AF-3492 was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident and Car bearing No.KA-05- MZ-7169 was not having Insurance policy as on the date of accident.
Further the drivers of both the vehicles were having driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the Goods Carrier vehicle in question was valid and was in force as on the date of accident.

26. Hence, the respondent no.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AF-3492 is liable to pay compensation to an extent of 80% and remaining 20%
compensation shall be paid by the respondent no.3 being the RC of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MZ-7169.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER  The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,48,348/- + cost of Rs.3,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.I.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.3,51,348/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Fifty One Thousand Three Hundred Forty Eight only).
d A Sum of Rs.3,48,348/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The Respondent No 2 is liable to pay 80% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.2,78,678/- +
cost of Rs.3000/- imposed vide order on IA No.I.

The respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the compensation of Rs.2,81,678/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Eighty One Thousand Six Hundred Seventy Eight only) with interest at 6% within 2 months from the date of this award.
